definition: The voice between tracks; in GTA IV and GTA V usually a real musician or DJ playing a version of themselves, such as Iggy Pop on Liberty Rock Radio or Flying Lotus on FlyLo FM.
A non-music satire station, such as Integrity 2.0 in GTA IV or West Coast Talk Radio and Blaine County Radio in GTA V.
The custom station in GTA IV on PC (and later Chinatown Wars on iOS and Android) that plays the player's own audio files.
GTA V's custom station for the player's own audio files, added with the PC version in April 2015.
The 2009 standalone bundle of GTA IV's two episodes, The Lost and Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony, with three exclusive stations.
The 2014 release of GTA V for newer consoles, which added about 165 radio tracks per the GTA wiki, 22 of them songs cut from the 2013 release.
Music rights are bought for a fixed term; when they lapse, songs are patched out, as happened to GTA IV from April 26, 2018.
A GTA Online station that plays only the mixes a player has collected on Media Sticks, added in Los Santos Tuners (2021).
In GTA Online: After Hours, a real DJ booked to play the player's nightclub, whose mix then airs on Los Santos Underground Radio.
A temporary playlist on an existing station, such as the Dre Day set on West Coast Classics, merged into its regular rotation in January 2022 per the GTA wiki.
Unreleased music first heard on a GTA station, such as The Voidz on Kult FM or Dr. Dre's tracks in The Contract.
